pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: P0 - Serving degradation detected for inference-runtime-prod. Symptoms: RDMA fabric flapping in rack-us-west-2a -> sustained packet loss and retransmits, causing CUDA timeouts, container restarts and downstream OOMs. Triggered at 2026-03-14T03:12:11Z.

Tessa (oncall): ack. I'm starting triage. Calling out infra + netops. Initial impact: increased 99.9p latency and ~8% 5xx on embeddings + generation routes. Will try traffic mitigation and node isolation.

Eli (runtime): seeing KV-cache eviction storm on the serving pods attached to the affected nodes. When retransmits spike we get akka backlog and then CUDA timeouts -> containers restart. My immediate mitigation: flip a portion of traffic to CPU fallback and turn off continuous batching. Applying a runtime routing change now:

```
# switch routing to cpu fallback (canary 30%)
redwoodctl routing set --service inference-runtime-prod --policy fallback:cpu --selector rack=us-west-2a --canary 0.3
# reduce batching / disable async kv cache
redwoodctl config set inference-runtime-prod BATCHING_ENABLED=false KVCACHE_ASYNC=false
```

Samir (infra): running RDMA checks against node-uw2a-n12..n15. ibv_rc_pingpong shows recv timeout / retry storms. Starting host-level isolation and warming up replacement nodes in us-west-2b. From the switch:

```
$ ibv_rc_pingpong 10.2.4.13
rc_pingpong: recv timeout (after retries)
$ ethtool -S mlx5_core | grep -i retransmit
mlx5_retransmits: 24190
```

Kai (sre): recommended plan: 1) cordon + drain the flapping hosts; 2) scale up capacity in another rack and steer traffic; 3) keep a smaller CPU fallback pool until NICs replaced. Commands I'll run: 

```
kubectl cordon node-uw2a-n13
kubectl drain node-uw2a-n13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n prod
kubectl scale deployment/inference-runtime --replicas=60 -n prod
```

Tessa (oncall): customer-impact summary for CS: peak window ~03:10-03:34 UTC saw 99.9p latency jump and 8% failure rate across embeddings endpoints. Affected customers: top10 enterprise tenants using embeddings. CS please prepare status page + direct emails.

Customer-success: drafting incident message and will post to status.redwood.ai. Will include mitigation steps and ETA for full recovery once infra confirms node replacements.

netops-bot: ALERT: IB_PORT_STATE changes observed on node-uw2a-n13 port1: LINK_DOWN -> LINK_UP flapping 12x in last 10m. Relevant logs: 

```
Mar 14 03:10:12 node-uw2a-n13 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:08:00.0: mlx5_core port 1 link down
Mar 14 03:10:22 node-uw2a-n13 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:08:00.0: mlx5_core port 1 link up
Mar 14 03:11:05 node-uw2a-n13 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:08:00.0: mlx5_core port 1 link down
```

Eli (runtime): I've also reduced token prefetch and disabled continuous KV prewarming to stop churn while we migrate traffic. Observed canary (30%) error rate drop to ~1.2% after initial switch.

Samir (infra): cloud provider contacted; they suspect NIC firmware causing link flaps and are provisioning replacement hosts. Provisioning ETA ~22 minutes. Meanwhile we're provisioning spare nodes in us-west-2b and increasing autoscaler headroom.

Kai (sre): performing controlled drain on n12-n15 in waves to avoid mass eviction. Rolling restarts of inference-runtime on replaced hosts once they report clean IB state. Temporary mitigations: increase request timeouts and reduce concurrency per pod.

Tessa (oncall): handing pager to kai for sustained monitoring / follow-up. Handoff notes: - routing changed to CPU fallback canary 30% - batching disabled for affected service - infra ticket created INC-8721 with cloud provider - CS notified top customers and status page update queued.

Kai (oncall): ack, taking over. Will keep thread pinned and post status every 30 minutes until all nodes replaced and error rates stable <0.5% for 30m. :thumbsup:
